name: IS corpus (your own conversions)
blurb: The India standards corpus, built on this PC from BIS PDFs you licensed yourself — IS 800, IS 801, IS 811, IS 808, IS 1161, IS 2062, IS 875 (Parts 1–5), IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 + Amd 1/2, IS 18168:2023 and the connection standards — with the full-text / exact-id search the design agents ground their clauses on. The hub ships the tooling only, never standard text: a fresh install is an EMPTY corpus. Workflow: (1) convert your PDFs (Admin → Standards, or Convert), Rebuild index, Validate corpus; (2) the corpus-fix step: zip the corpus folder with your PDFs and CORPUS_FIX_LLM_INSTRUCTIONS.md for a frontier LLM agent with code execution; (3) Import fixed corpus. No vector DB; nothing leaves this PC unless you send it.

post_install:
import shutil,pathlib,os,stat,subprocess,sys
mod=pathlib.Path(r"{module_dir}"); src=mod/"scripts"; dst=pathlib.Path(r"{data_dir}")/"grokbot"

# ---- 1. the workspace corpus, EMPTY on a fresh install ---------------------------------------
# The hub ships the corpus tooling only -- no BIS text, tables, figures or transcriptions. You build
# the corpus from your own licensed PDFs. An existing workspace (documents you converted, a fixed
# corpus you imported) is kept as it is: nothing below deletes or overwrites corpus data.
for d in ("documents/standards","queue/in","queue/out","queue/done","cache","indexes","search","pdfs"):
    (dst/d).mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)

# ---- 2. the bundled tooling: code always refreshed, data files only seeded --------------------
# *.py are copied every time (code always wins; the tabs and the grounding server run from the
# workspace, and retrieval.find_root expects scripts/ beside documents/). Data files (*.json:
# aliases.json, and the corpus-fix data such as quality.json) are copied only when missing, so an
# update never replaces what the corpus-fix step gave you. Read-only bits are cleared first,
# because copytree leaves a read-only destination in place without a word.
(dst/"scripts").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
replaced, failed = [], []
for f in sorted(src.rglob("*")):
    if f.is_dir() or "__pycache__" in f.parts:
        continue
    t = dst/"scripts"/f.relative_to(src)
    t.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if t.is_file() and (f.suffix != ".py" or (t.stat().st_size == f.stat().st_size and t.read_bytes() == f.read_bytes())):
        continue
    try:
        if t.exists():
            os.chmod(t, stat.S_IWRITE | stat.S_IREAD)
        shutil.copy2(f, t)
        replaced.append(f.name)
    except OSError as e:
        failed.append(f"{f.name} ({e.__class__.__name__})")
if replaced:
    print("[is-corpus] workspace scripts refreshed:", ", ".join(replaced))
if failed:
    print("[is-corpus] COULD NOT REFRESH:", ", ".join(failed))
    raise SystemExit("[is-corpus] the workspace code is older than the module -- queries would use the OLD code")

# ---- 3. prove it, rather than assume it --------------------------------------------------------
stale=[n for n in ("retrieval.py","build_index.py","search.py","query_cache.py","pipeline_fixes.py","validate.py","import_corpus_zip.py")
       if (src/n).is_file() and (not (dst/"scripts"/n).is_file() or (src/n).read_bytes() != (dst/"scripts"/n).read_bytes())]
if stale:
    raise SystemExit("[is-corpus] workspace code does not match the module: " + ", ".join(stale))

# ---- 4. an index, even an empty one, so the grounding server starts and answers "not in the corpus"
if not (dst/"search"/"spec_fts.sqlite").is_file() or not (dst/"indexes"/"documents.json").is_file():
    rc = subprocess.call([sys.executable, str(dst/"scripts"/"build_index.py"), "--root", str(dst), "--no-repair"],
                         stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, cwd=str(dst))
    print("[is-corpus] index built" if rc == 0 else f"[is-corpus] WARNING: build_index.py exited {rc} (run Rebuild index)")

std = dst/"documents"/"standards"
n = sum(1 for d in std.iterdir() if d.is_dir())
print("[is-corpus] workspace ready at", dst, "--", n, "document folders")
if n == 0:
    print("[is-corpus] The corpus is EMPTY. The hub ships no standard text: build it from BIS PDFs you licensed yourself.")
    print("[is-corpus]   1. Admin -> Standards (a folder of PDFs) or IS corpus -> Convert (one PDF); then Rebuild index, Validate corpus")
    print("[is-corpus]   2. corpus-fix step: zip", dst, "with your PDFs and CORPUS_FIX_LLM_INSTRUCTIONS.md for an LLM agent")
    print("[is-corpus]   3. IS corpus -> Import fixed corpus (it rebuilds the index and validates)")

converter.label: PDF converter (Docling 2.123.1)
converter.help: Needed to convert your own licensed BIS PDFs — the hub ships no converted documents. Large download (ML stack). The corpus tooling pins 2.123.1 — do not upgrade without revalidating retrieval accuracy. The [rapidocr] extra adds onnxruntime, which convert_pdf.py's RapidOCR fallback needs on the scanned BIS prints (IS 801, IS 811, IS 816, IS 875-5).

tabs.title: Corpus
tabs.blurb: What this machine has: the BIS documents you converted, their edition, collection name and quality grade, the FTS index and the last validation. Run this first. The hub ships no standard text, so a fresh install shows an EMPTY corpus and the three steps that build it: convert your licensed PDFs, the corpus-fix step (CORPUS_FIX_LLM_INSTRUCTIONS.md), Import fixed corpus.

run.label: Check corpus

tabs.title: Query
tabs.blurb: Verbatim excerpts from the converted BIS documents. `found: false` is an honest answer — nothing is paraphrased or invented; a US term (SDS, Cd, Ω0 …) answers found:false with the IS equivalent, and a town in neither IS 875-3 Annex A nor IS 1893 Annex E answers not_tabulated (read the map). Every hit is standard text (BIS documents carry no separate commentary); always verify numbers against the PDF page the hit names — formula text from OCR / Docling can be garbled, and a hand-typed Canonical line follows the clause where it matters.

fields.label: Project
fields.help: Queries are logged to this project's folder.

options.label: Table id (or a section designation: HB 300, MC 175)

fields.label: Query
fields.placeholder: e.g. 7.1.2   ·   Table 9   ·   basic wind speed Chennai   ·   HB 300   ·   importance factor hospital

fields.label: Document
fields.help: Canonical stems, fixed by the corpus (retrieval ids depend on them). A collection name (engineering_standards_IS800) is accepted too.

options.label: IS 875 (Part 4):2021 snow (stem keeps its historical name)

fields.label: Include commentary (none in BIS documents — kept for parity)
fields.help: BIS documents carry no separate commentary volume: every India hit is part=standard. Off by default.

tabs.title: Convert PDF
tabs.blurb: Convert a BIS PDF you licensed yourself with Docling at full accuracy (TableFormer ACCURATE, formula enrichment on, OCR fallback for scanned prints), post-processed with the is_bis profile; the output lands in documents/standards/<STEM>. This is the first pass of the corpus: every document the agents ground on comes from here (or from Admin → Standards, which queues a folder of PDFs through this tab). Needs the optional component "PDF converter (Docling 2.123.1)" — install it once from the Modules tab (large download, the ML stack); the hub refuses to run this tab until it is present. Then run Rebuild index and Validate corpus, and the corpus-fix step (CORPUS_FIX_LLM_INSTRUCTIONS.md) for what a first pass gets wrong. The licence watermark of BIS PDFs is stripped by the post-processing (strip_watermark.py --check reports what remains).

run.label: Convert
run.crash_hint: Convert again with the same stem -- it resumes from the last finished chunk (the log shows 'Resume: reusing existing chunk pages'). If it dies at the same place twice, lower Pages per chunk (5 -> 2) or use Page range to isolate the page; a memory-hungry page in PyTorch or onnxruntime is the usual cause.

fields.label: Specification PDF
fields.help: Your own licensed BIS copy. Nothing is uploaded anywhere — conversion runs on this machine.

fields.label: Canonical stem
fields.help: Must match exactly: the retrieval ids and the collection map (engineering_standards_IS*) are keyed on these stems.

options.label: IS 875 (Part 4):2021 snow (stem keeps its historical name)

fields.label: Pages per chunk
fields.help: 5 is the documented default. Lower it only to work around out-of-memory, never to gain speed.

tabs.title: Re-process
tabs.blurb: Rebuild one converted document's searchable markdown, sections, equations and tables from the Docling chunks already on disk — no re-conversion, minutes not hours. Use it after a tooling update, or when a document's text looks like another's. Pick the stem, and give it the source PDF if you have it (equation ids, table captions and ligature repair all read it), then run Rebuild index.

run.label: Re-process document
run.crash_hint: Re-processing reads the PDF only for the equation census; if it died there, run it again with the source PDF left blank.

fields.label: Converted document
fields.help: The converted document's folder under documents/standards (the Corpus tab lists them).

options.label: IS 875 (Part 4):2021 snow (stem keeps its historical name)

fields.label: Source PDF (optional)
fields.help: Only needed for the equation census. Leave empty to skip it.

tabs.title: Rebuild index
tabs.blurb: Rebuild the unified indexes (sections, tables, equations, documents with edition and quality) and the FTS index after converting, re-processing or importing: the per-document BIS index repair (only where the source PDF is found: its recorded path, $INDIA_PDF_DIRS or <corpus>/pdfs/<STEM>.pdf), then the unified build. Tick "Skip the per-document repair" after importing a fixed corpus, so its indexes are kept as they came. Follow it with Validate corpus.

fields.label: Skip the per-document repair (keep the indexes as they are)
fields.help: For a corpus fixed by the corpus-fix step and imported: the repair re-derives the per-document indexes from the PDF text layer and could undo index fixes.

tabs.title: Validate corpus
tabs.blurb: The corpus's must-hit probes (validate.py --corpus) for every document you converted (the others are skipped): clause and table ids the agents ask for most (IS 1893 7.2.6 / Table 9, IS 800 7.1.2.1 / Annex D, IS 875-3 6.3.4, IS 18168 5.5 …) with short key-phrase checks, the town lookup, the "not in the corpus" note, the US-term trap, and a grep that no licence watermark line survives in any text artefact. Advisory [corpus-fix] lines report what the corpus-fix step normally adds (figure transcriptions, section-property rows). Exit 1 = the build is not usable; a first pass often fails some probes — that is what the corpus-fix step is for. Rebuild index first.

tabs.title: Import fixed corpus
tabs.blurb: Step 3 of the workflow: put the fixed corpus zip returned by the corpus-fix step (CORPUS_FIX_LLM_INSTRUCTIONS.md) in place of this PC's corpus. The zip is checked first (documents/standards/<STEM>/ at the top or under one folder; unsafe paths refused), the grounding server is stopped, the current documents/, indexes/, search/, cache/ and scripts/*.json go to <data>/grokbot_backups/<time>/ (move them back to undo), and the zip's are moved in. The hub's code is never replaced: scripts/*.py in the zip are kept aside in the backup for review, scripts/*.json (quality.json and the other corpus data) are applied, PDFs are ignored. Then Rebuild index (no repair) and Validate corpus run, and the server starts again.

fields.label: Fixed corpus zip
fields.help: The zip the LLM agent returned. Nothing is uploaded anywhere — it is unpacked on this machine.

fields.label: Rebuild index (no repair) and Validate corpus afterwards

tabs.title: Retrieval plan
tabs.blurb: Run a whole retrieval plan at once — the batch path an agent uses to fill a load_plan or nl_plan from many clause queries (serve_queue.py --plan).

fields.label: Plan JSON
fields.help: {plan_id, submitted, queries:[{qid, doc, type, query, purpose, want_commentary, context_neighbors}]}

tabs.title: Grounding
tabs.blurb: What the design agents are asking this corpus, and what they got back. HR Steel (IS 800), CFS (IS 801) and the Nonlinear Review point their standards search here automatically (RAG_API_URL). An empty corpus answers every question "not in the corpus" — the agents then cite from memory and flag every value.
